slides.title: The interrupt — hardware makes the call
Summary: What You'll Need In Class
items: A timer counts at a rate that depends on the system clock and the prescaler.
The amount of time that has passed is counting rate times count.
When count reaches the auto-reload value, the timer hardware resets to 0 and generates and update event. (Other behaviors are possible here as well.)
A timer interrupt is initiated by the hardware, and it can happen at any time during regular code execution.
The ISR (interrupt service routine) is code you write and to which the processor jumps at the time the interrupt fires.
Important about the ISR: exact name, quick in and out, volatile on anything shared.
In class we will build all of it: Blinky with no delay_ms() anywhere.
